strategy_title: libdevice.fma for BN Affine Chain Regresses Despite FMA Fusion
strategy_description: Replacing a two-step multiply-add (tmp53 = tmp51 * tmp52; tmp55 = tmp53 + tmp54) with libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54) in a Triton batchnorm affine transform reduced registers per thread from 32 to 26 and improved achieved occupancy from 78.1% to 83.3%, but simultaneously increased executed instructions from 24.1M to 29.9M (+24%) and elapsed cycles from 64K to 73K, causing a net slowdown (duration 42.82 µs → 49.22 µs). The instruction count increase suggests the compiler expanded the fma call into additional bookkeeping or the xmask change from tl.full([XBLOCK], True) to xindex < xnumel added predication overhead across all loads and stores. The FPInstructions NCU rule remained present after the change, indicating the fused instruction count did not improve as expected.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: registers=32/thread, Duration=42.82us, Executed=24.1M inst
xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]  # no boundary check
tmp53 = tmp51 * tmp52
tmp55 = tmp53 + tmp54  # separate FMUL + FADD
tmp57 = tl.maximum(tmp56, tmp55)
tl.store(in_out_ptr0 + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (REGRESSION): registers=26/thread, Duration=49.22us, Executed=29.9M inst
xmask = xindex < xnumel  # boundary predication added to ALL loads/stores
tmp55 = libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54)  # single FFMA
tmp57 = tl.maximum(tmp56, tmp55)
tl.store(in_out_ptr0 + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
applicable_when: Never apply as described: replacing a two-step mul+add with libdevice.fma while simultaneously changing xmask from tl.full([XBLOCK], True) to xindex < xnumel causes instruction count to balloon due to added predication overhead on all memory operations, negating any FMA fusion benefit.
do_not_apply_when: When the kernel already uses xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] (i.e., xnumel is divisible by XBLOCK and no boundary masking is needed), do NOT change the xmask pattern while applying libdevice.fma. The predication overhead from switching to xindex < xnumel adds masked instructions to every load and store, increasing total instruction count by ~24% and more than offsetting any FMA fusion savings. Also do not apply if the FPInstructions NCU rule's non-fused ops originate from branches other than the targeted mul+add pair.
framework_notes: In Triton, the diff shows two simultaneous changes: (1) xmask changed from tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] to xindex < xnumel, and (2) XBLOCK changed from a constexpr default to a bare constexpr (removing the default=128). The xmask change is the likely culprit for the instruction count increase: it adds predication to all tl.load and tl.store calls, generating extra predicate register usage and conditional instructions. If applying libdevice.fma, keep xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] unchanged to isolate the FMA effect.

strategy_title: XBLOCK=256 + True Mask + FMA Reduces Instructions, Improves Duration
strategy_description: In a Triton pointwise kernel where xnumel is exactly divisible by XBLOCK=256, replacing the boundary predicate (xindex < xnumel) with tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] eliminates predication overhead from all loads and stores, and simultaneously dropping the outer xmask conjunction from per-branch conditional masks (keeping only the branch predicate itself) reduces executed instructions from 29.9M to 24.1M (-19%). Adding libdevice.fma for the batchnorm affine multiply-add further fuses two FP32 instructions into one. Together these changes reduced kernel duration from 48.77 µs to 42.34 µs (1.26x speedup) despite registers per thread increasing from 26 to 32 and achieved occupancy dropping from 83.1% to 77.5%, demonstrating that instruction count reduction can outweigh occupancy loss when the kernel is instruction-throughput-bound rather than latency-bound.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=256, num_warps=8, registers=26/thread
# xmask = xindex < xnumel  (boundary predication on all ops)
# Achieved Occupancy=83.1%, Executed=29.9M inst, Duration=48.77us
xmask = xindex < xnumel
xmask4 = xmask & tmp4
tmp5 = tl.load(ptr0 + ..., mask=xmask4, eviction_policy='evict_last', other=0.0)
# ... 6 more conditional loads with xmask & branch_pred ...
tmp41 = tl.load(ptr7 + x0, mask=xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
# ...
tmp53 = tmp51 * tmp52
tmp55 = tmp53 + tmp54
tl.store(out + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
fast_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=256, num_warps=8, registers=32/thread
# xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]  (no boundary check)
# Achieved Occupancy=77.5%, Executed=24.1M inst, Duration=42.34us
xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]
tmp5 = tl.load(ptr0 + ..., mask=tmp4, eviction_policy='evict_last', other=0.0)  # outer xmask dropped
# ... 6 more conditional loads with branch_pred only ...
tmp41 = tl.load(ptr7 + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')  # no mask
# ...
tmp55 = libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54)  # fused multiply-add
tl.store(out + x2, tmp57)  # no mask
applicable_when: Triton pointwise kernel where: (1) xnumel is exactly divisible by XBLOCK so boundary masking is unnecessary; (2) the kernel uses xindex < xnumel predication that adds mask arguments to all loads/stores; (3) per-branch conditional masks are conjunctions of the outer xmask with a branch predicate (xmask & tmp_branch), allowing the outer xmask to be dropped when it is always True; (4) the kernel contains a batchnorm-style affine chain (mul + add) that can be fused into FMA; (5) executed instruction count is the primary bottleneck rather than memory latency.
do_not_apply_when: xnumel is NOT exactly divisible by XBLOCK (boundary masking is required for correctness). Do not drop the outer xmask conjunction from per-branch conditional masks if xmask is not always True. Do not apply if the kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound (DRAM Throughput > 60%) rather than instruction-throughput-bound, as the instruction reduction benefit will be smaller. Be aware that this change increased registers per thread from 26 to 32 in this instance, which may reduce theoretical occupancy if Block Limit Registers becomes the binding limiter.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] as the xmask eliminates all predication overhead when xnumel % XBLOCK == 0. Per-branch conditional masks of the form (xmask & branch_pred) can be simplified to just branch_pred when xmask is always True, reducing live variable count. libdevice.fma(a, b, c) computes a*b+c as a single FFMA instruction. The combination of true-mask + FMA reduced executed instructions by ~19% (29.9M → 24.1M) and duration by ~13% despite a register increase from 26 to 32/thread.

strategy_title: Replace xindex<xnumel Mask with tl.full True to Cut Instructions
strategy_description: When xnumel is exactly divisible by XBLOCK, replacing the runtime boundary check `xmask = xindex < xnumel` with the compile-time constant `xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]` eliminates predication from every load and store, reducing executed instructions by ~19% (29.9M → 24.1M) and kernel duration by ~13% (48.77 µs → 42.37 µs). The FPInstructions NCU rule flags this pattern because predicated instructions inflate non-fused FP32 instruction counts; removing the predication allows the compiler to emit unconditional PTX load/store instructions. Note that registers per thread increased from 26 to 32 (a side effect of the autotune config change), but the instruction count reduction dominated and produced a net speedup.
slow_pseudocode:
# xnumel divisible by XBLOCK, but runtime boundary check used
xmask = xindex < xnumel  # adds predication to ALL loads/stores
tmp5 = tl.load(ptr0 + ..., mask=tmp4 & xmask, ...)  # compound predicate
tmp41 = tl.load(ptr7 + x0, mask=xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')  # scalar load with mask
tl.store(out + x2, result, mask=xmask)  # store with mask
# Executed Instructions: 29.9M, Duration: 48.77 us
fast_pseudocode:
# xnumel divisible by XBLOCK, compile-time True mask used
xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]  # no boundary check
tmp5 = tl.load(ptr0 + ..., mask=tmp4, ...)  # branch predicate only, no xmask
tmp41 = tl.load(ptr7 + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')  # scalar load, no mask
tl.store(out + x2, result)  # unconditional store
# Executed Instructions: 24.1M, Duration: 42.37 us
applicable_when: xnumel is exactly divisible by all XBLOCK values in the autotune configs (verified: xnumel % XBLOCK == 0 for every config). The FPInstructions NCU rule is triggered with elevated non-fused instruction counts. The kernel uses `xmask = xindex < xnumel` and passes xmask (or compound predicates like tmp4 & xmask) to tl.load and tl.store mask arguments. Executed instruction count is anomalously high relative to the number of memory operations.
do_not_apply_when: xnumel is NOT exactly divisible by XBLOCK for all autotune configs — removing the boundary mask will cause out-of-bounds memory accesses and incorrect results. Do not apply if the kernel already uses tl.full([XBLOCK], True) masking. Do not apply if the instruction count inflation is caused by something other than predication (e.g., register spilling, branch divergence).
framework_notes: In Triton, `xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]` signals to the compiler that the mask is always True, causing it to emit unconditional PTX ld/st instructions instead of predicated @P0 variants. For compound masks like `tmp4 & xmask` where xmask is always True, the & xmask term can be dropped entirely, leaving only the branch predicate (tmp4). For scalar evict_last loads that only used xmask (not a branch predicate), the mask= argument can be removed entirely. This pattern is safe only when xnumel % XBLOCK == 0 for every config in the autotune decorator.

strategy_title: Small XBLOCK + num_stages=1 + FMA + tl.full Mask Reduces Instructions
strategy_description: Combining @triton.autotune configs restricted to XBLOCK=64/128 with num_stages=1, replacing a two-step multiply-add (tmp53=tmp51*tmp52; tmp55=tmp53+tmp54) with libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54), and keeping xmask as tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] reduced executed instructions from 29.9M to 24.1M (~19% reduction) and elapsed cycles from 72958 to 63486, yielding a 1.26x speedup. Critically, the xmask must remain as tl.full (not xindex < xnumel) to avoid adding predication overhead to all loads and stores — prior experiments (exp_003) showed that switching to xindex < xnumel while applying FMA caused instruction count to increase by 24% and negated the FMA benefit entirely. The FPInstructions NCU rule (flagging non-fused FP32 ops) is the correct signal to target with libdevice.fma, but only when the xmask pattern is preserved.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=64..128, num_stages=1, tl.full xmask, two-step mul+add
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 128}, num_warps=4, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 128}, num_warps=2, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 64},  num_warps=4, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 64},  num_warps=2, num_stages=1),
], key=['xnumel'])
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]
    # ... 7-way tl.where concat + batchnorm ...
    tmp50 = tl.rsqrt(tmp45)
    tmp51 = tmp42 * tmp50
    tmp53 = tmp51 * tmp52   # FMUL
    tmp55 = tmp53 + tmp54   # FADD (non-fused)
    tmp57 = tl.maximum(tmp56, tmp55)
    tl.store(out + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
fast_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=64..128, num_stages=1, tl.full xmask, fused FMA
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 128}, num_warps=4, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 128}, num_warps=2, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 64},  num_warps=4, num_stages=1),
    triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 64},  num_warps=2, num_stages=1),
], key=['xnumel'])
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]  # MUST keep tl.full, not xindex < xnumel
    # ... 7-way tl.where concat + batchnorm ...
    tmp50 = tl.rsqrt(tmp45)
    tmp51 = tmp42 * tmp50
    tmp55 = libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54)  # single FFMA, eliminates tmp53
    tmp57 = tl.maximum(tmp56, tmp55)
    tl.store(out + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
applicable_when: Triton pointwise kernel with FPInstructions NCU rule triggered (non-fused FP32 multiply-add pairs present), xnumel divisible by XBLOCK (so tl.full mask is safe), autotune already restricted to XBLOCK<=128 with num_stages=1, and xmask is already tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]. The kernel contains a batchnorm-style affine transform (scale * normalized + bias) expressed as two separate instructions.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply libdevice.fma while simultaneously changing xmask from tl.full([XBLOCK], True) to xindex < xnumel — the predication overhead on all loads/stores will increase instruction count by ~24% and negate the FMA benefit (confirmed by exp_003). Do not apply if xnumel is not divisible by XBLOCK (boundary masking is required for correctness). Do not apply if registers per thread would exceed 32 (Block Limit Registers would drop below 16).
framework_notes: libdevice.fma(a, b, c) computes a*b+c as a single FFMA instruction, equivalent to the two-step (tmp = a*b; result = tmp+c) pattern. Requires 'from triton.language.extra import libdevice'. The key correctness constraint is that xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] must be preserved when xnumel % XBLOCK == 0 — switching to xindex < xnumel adds predication to every tl.load and tl.store, increasing instruction count more than the FMA saves. tl.rsqrt and libdevice.rsqrt are interchangeable single-instruction reciprocal square roots.

strategy_title: evict_first on Streaming Inputs Preserves Small Reused Tensors in Cache
strategy_description: When a kernel loads large streaming tensors (each accessed once per CTA) alongside small frequently-reused parameter tensors (e.g., batchnorm weight/bias/mean/var, ~1KB total), marking the large streaming loads with eviction_policy='evict_first' (cache-streaming hint, maps to PTX .cs) prevents them from evicting the small reused tensors from L1/L2. In this case, DRAM throughput dropped from 18.95% to 16.28% and Average DRAM Active Cycles fell from 29,537 to 25,305 (~14% reduction), indicating the BN parameter tensors were better retained in cache. The overall speedup was modest (1.10x, ~0.16 µs reduction) because the kernel is primarily compute-bound (Compute SOL ~78%) and the memory improvement only partially addresses the 18% scheduler no-eligible stall.
slow_pseudocode:
# Large streaming inputs (loaded once per CTA) use evict_last (cache-all)
tmp5  = tl.load(in_ptr0 + offset0, mask=mask0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp10 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + offset1, mask=mask1, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp15 = tl.load(in_ptr2 + offset2, mask=mask2, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp20 = tl.load(in_ptr3 + offset3, mask=mask3, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp25 = tl.load(in_ptr4 + offset4, mask=mask4, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp30 = tl.load(in_ptr5 + offset5, mask=mask5, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp34 = tl.load(in_ptr6 + offset6, mask=mask6, eviction_policy='evict_last')
# Small BN params (256 floats each, reused across all CTAs) also use evict_last
tmp41 = tl.load(bn_mean  + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp43 = tl.load(bn_var   + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp52 = tl.load(bn_weight+ x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp54 = tl.load(bn_bias  + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
fast_pseudocode:
# Large streaming inputs switched to evict_first (cache-streaming, .cs hint)
tmp5  = tl.load(in_ptr0 + offset0, mask=mask0, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp10 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + offset1, mask=mask1, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp15 = tl.load(in_ptr2 + offset2, mask=mask2, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp20 = tl.load(in_ptr3 + offset3, mask=mask3, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp25 = tl.load(in_ptr4 + offset4, mask=mask4, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp30 = tl.load(in_ptr5 + offset5, mask=mask5, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp34 = tl.load(in_ptr6 + offset6, mask=mask6, eviction_policy='evict_first')
# Small BN params kept as evict_last to maximize L1/L2 residency
tmp41 = tl.load(bn_mean  + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp43 = tl.load(bn_var   + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp52 = tl.load(bn_weight+ x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp54 = tl.load(bn_bias  + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
applicable_when: Kernel loads multiple large streaming tensors (each element read once per CTA, no reuse) alongside small parameter tensors (e.g., BN weight/bias/mean/var, <4KB total) that are reused across all CTAs at the same offsets. DRAM Throughput is non-trivial (>10%), L2 Hit Rate is moderate (~50%), and the kernel has many concurrent CTAs (high waves_per_sm). The small parameter tensors are being evicted from L1/L2 by the large streaming inputs.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is purely compute-bound with negligible DRAM traffic (DRAM Throughput <5%), or all tensors are large streaming with no reused small tensors to protect. Do not apply when the large inputs are actually reused across multiple CTAs (e.g., weight matrices in GEMM). Speedup is limited when the kernel is already compute-bound (Compute SOL >75%); expect only modest gains (~5-15% DRAM reduction, <5% overall latency improvement).
framework_notes: In Triton, eviction_policy='evict_first' maps to PTX cache hint .cs (cache streaming), which marks the cache line as low-priority for eviction immediately after use. eviction_policy='evict_last' maps to .ca (cache all), marking it as high-priority. This is a pure cache hint with no effect on correctness. In CUDA C++, the equivalent is using __ldcs() for streaming loads vs. __ldcg() or regular loads for reused data. The change is zero-cost in terms of instruction count and register usage.

strategy_title: num_warps=4 + evict_first Regresses When xmask Predication Added
strategy_description: Combining num_warps=4 (via autotune), evict_first on streaming loads, and switching xmask from tl.full([XBLOCK], True) to xindex < xnumel produced a net regression relative to the prior best (42.34 µs → 48.42 µs, +14% duration), despite improving achieved occupancy from 77.5% to 83.4% and reducing DRAM throughput from 21.84% to 16.35%. The root cause is that changing xmask to xindex < xnumel added boundary predication to all loads and stores, increasing executed instructions from 24.1M to 29.9M (+24%), which more than offset any benefit from the warp reduction and eviction policy changes. The speedup of 1.1057x reported is relative to an earlier baseline (48.77 µs), not the true best (42.34 µs); against the true best this is a regression of ~0.87x.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (true best): tl.full xmask, no autotune, registers=32/thread
# Duration=42.34us, Executed=24.1M inst, Achieved Occupancy=77.5%
xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:]
tmp5 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + ..., mask=tmp4, eviction_policy='evict_last')
# ... 6 more streaming loads with branch_pred only ...
tmp41 = tl.load(bn_mean + x0, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp55 = libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54)
tl.store(out + x2, tmp57)  # no mask
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128),)
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regression): xindex<xnumel xmask, autotune num_warps=4, registers=26/thread
# Duration=48.42us, Executed=29.9M inst, Achieved Occupancy=83.4%
@triton.autotune(configs=[triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 128}, num_warps=4, num_stages=3)], key=['xnumel'])
def kernel(...):
    xmask = xindex < xnumel  # REGRESSION: adds predication to all ops
    xmask4 = xmask & tmp4
    tmp5 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + ..., mask=xmask4, eviction_policy='evict_first')
    # ... 6 more streaming loads with xmask & branch_pred ...
    tmp41 = tl.load(bn_mean + x0, mask=xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
    tmp55 = libdevice.fma(tmp51, tmp52, tmp54)
    tl.store(out + x2, tmp57, mask=xmask)
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128),)
kernel[grid](...)  # autotune selects config
applicable_when: Never apply this combined pattern. The evict_first direction alone (without xmask change) is captured in exp_004_evict_first_streaming_loads_preserve_bn_params_in_cache and gives modest gains. The num_warps reduction alone may help if xmask is kept as tl.full.
do_not_apply_when: Do NOT combine evict_first streaming loads with a change from tl.full([XBLOCK], True) xmask to xindex < xnumel. The predication overhead from the xmask change increases executed instructions by ~24% and causes a net regression even when occupancy improves. Do not apply when the kernel already uses tl.full([XBLOCK], True) masking and the true best baseline is at 42.34 µs — any change that reintroduces xindex < xnumel will regress.
framework_notes: In Triton, the xmask pattern is the dominant factor: tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)[:] eliminates all predication overhead (safe when xnumel % XBLOCK == 0), while xindex < xnumel adds predicated instructions to every load and store. The num_warps=4 change via autotune also introduced num_stages=3 which may have added software pipelining overhead. The evict_first policy change itself is beneficial (DRAM throughput dropped from 21.84% to 16.35%), but was masked by the instruction count regression from the xmask change.
